title: Lookup in a concatenation of equal-length lists
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers and let $f$ assign a list to each natural number less than $n$, with every such list having length $k$. For $i<n$, a natural number $r<k$, and a default element $d$, the entry at position $ik+r$ in the concatenation of these lists, with default $d$, equals the entry at position $r$ in the list assigned to $i$, with the same default.
hypotheses_covered: A list-valued function $f$ on indices less than $n$
A default element $d$ of the list type
